items.evidence: final.md:5 names CBZ with evidence ('CbzLoader overrides load() and never calls normalizeMetadata() (the option would be dead)') and FB2 ('Fb2Loader already preserves author-sort via its own override'); EPUB covered via inheritance. But PDF is never named as executing the base step at runtime — it appears only in the lumped claim 'pdf, txt, cbz, fb2: byte-for-byte identical output' (final.md:13); TXT is named only as having 'no author-sort to preserve' without stating it executes the shared step.

final.md:5 explicitly distinguishes runtime behavior from inheritance: 'CbzLoader overrides load() and never calls normalizeMetadata()' and 'Fb2Loader already preserves author-sort via its own override' — registry dispatch in viewer.js is never cited as proof CBZ or FB2 run the shared step.

final.md:5 rejects the interface-wide threading for the proven-unreachable and already-preserving consumers: threading 'through *all five* loaders is unnecessary churn' because for CBZ 'the option would be dead' and 'Fb2Loader already preserves author-sort via its own override'. patch.diff only wires the option into EpubLoader.

final.md:13 claims 'pdf, txt, cbz, fb2: byte-for-byte identical output to before (no behavior changes outside EPUB)' and line 5 asserts 'Only EPUB is affected'. The PDF sample carries author-sort 'Zola, Émile' distinct from author 'Émile Zola', so a shared-boundary fix must change PDF output; the run never reports this and the oracle (run.json exit 1) rejects exactly that claim.

The fix lands at the shared boundary (patch rewrites Loader.normalizeMetadata) and reuses the existing pipeline. But it adds precisely the prohibited 'new option surface': a preserveAuthorSort constructor option gated so only EPUB enables it, instead of fixing the boundary to preserve author-sort by default.

TXT is shown unaffected with a representative input (final.md:13, samples/book.txt has no author-sort). But the intended PDF change is not reported — final.md:13 instead asserts PDF unchanged ('no behavior changes outside EPUB'), contradicting the oracle.

Distinguishes flag existence from consumption for the proposed option in CBZ ('the option would be dead', final.md:5). But never checks the FB2 legacy flag path that no caller enables (fixture fb2.js 'useLegacyNormalize' is never mentioned in final.md or patch.diff).

EPUB gets its own concrete evidence (final.md:12), but pdf/txt/cbz/fb2 are lumped into a single 'byte-for-byte identical output' claim from one viewer.openBook check (final.md:11-13) — the per-format separation the rubric demands is absent for four of five formats.
